company.founder: Guglielmo Papaleo (Catanzaro). Named Cavaliere del Lavoro (Order of Merit for Labour) in 1997. Died May 2003 (sources give 5 May and 10 May - exact day UNVERIFIED).
company.founded_note: Official brand date is 1943 (company timeline, Italian Wikipedia, company press boilerplate "Creata nel 1943"). Some sources say 1945 for the Corso Mazzini shop (English Wikipedia, eccellenzecalabresi.it, beverfood 2008). Coffee production and sale began in 1947.
company.headquarters_and_plant: Località Copanello 1, 88071 Stalettì (CZ), Calabria, Italy - on the Ionian coast a few km from Catanzaro
commercial_offices: Copanello di Stalettì (Central and Southern Italy)
other_branches: Vimodrone (MI) distribution office for Lombardy (official e-shop, via search index)

phases: Green coffee cleaned of impurities (leaves, twigs, stones) and checked by specialists for organoleptic quality
Roasting in drum roasters at up to about 300 °C, with roast time set for each origin
Blending of the roasted Arabica and Robusta origins into each recipe
Grinding and packing: vacuum bricks, valve pouches in protective atmosphere, tins, capsules, ESE pods, whole beans
production.roasting_method: Origins are roasted separately and blended after roasting (official "Passion and research" page; Guglielmo USA production page). Wikipedia adds: methane-fired rotating-drum roasters, about 240-300 °C, 15-20 minutes, air-cooled (UNVERIFIED by the official site).
production.infrastructure_unverified: Two newer roasters, an 18 m outdoor green-coffee silo with 14 cells (about 3,300 sacks), green-bean cleaning machine and roasted-coffee silo installed from 1997 onward (English Wikipedia; UNVERIFIED).
production.green_coffee_origins: Brazil, Central America, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Vietnam among others (official e-shop homepage via search index; UNVERIFIED as complete list)

timeline.title: Apprentice in Catanzaro
timeline.text: Guglielmo Papaleo starts as a shop boy in a grocery in the old town of Catanzaro, learning the trade.

timeline.title: A shop and a coffee machine
timeline.text: Papaleo opens his own small shop on Corso Mazzini, Catanzaro, with a small coffee machine inside. The brand counts its history from this year (some sources say 1945).

timeline.title: Coffee becomes the business
timeline.text: Production and sale of coffee begin; the shop is enlarged so customers can taste the coffee on the spot.

timeline.title: The first Guglielmo bar
timeline.text: The first Guglielmo coffee bar opens (Italian Wikipedia; official timeline).

timeline.title: Stratò and the coffee-pot vans
timeline.text: The business moves to the Stratò district of Catanzaro and sells across the province, promoted by advertising vans shaped like a coffee pot with cups.

timeline.title: First roasting plant
timeline.text: Rising demand leads to the first roasting plant in Catanzaro Sala, with customs warehouses, production and offices (English Wikipedia says 1960).

timeline.title: Building Copanello
timeline.text: Construction begins on a new industrial complex at Copanello, on the Ionian coast.

timeline.title: Copanello opens, S.p.A. is born
timeline.text: The Copanello plant is inaugurated with modern machinery and the company becomes a joint-stock company (S.p.A.). (English Wikipedia dates the move to 1970.)

timeline.title: A second generation joins
timeline.text: Roberto Volpi, Papaleo's son-in-law, joins from Milan and becomes managing director.

timeline.title: The target logo
timeline.text: The concentric-target roundel and slogan "il caffè che fa centro" replace the earlier William Tell logo (Wikipedia date; the official timeline places the new identity in 1972-1987).

timeline.title: Cavaliere del Lavoro and 50 years
timeline.text: Guglielmo Papaleo is named Cavaliere del Lavoro and the company celebrates 50 years of coffee production; grandson Daniele Rossi joins the firm.

timeline.title: Export begins in earnest
timeline.text: Grandson Matteo Tubertini joins to lead exports into Europe and builds the partnership with the US importer, L'Espresso USA (English Wikipedia).

timeline.title: L'Espresso USA in Boston
timeline.text: Mimmo (Domenico) Elia founds L'Espresso USA in Boston to import and distribute Caffè Guglielmo.

timeline.title: Looking abroad
timeline.text: Guglielmo decides to invest in foreign markets and, in 2001-2002, begins exhibiting at major coffee trade fairs in Portugal and Germany.

timeline.title: Canada, and a farewell
timeline.text: L'Espresso USA expands into Canada. In May 2003 founder Guglielmo Papaleo passes away.

timeline.title: Espresso Italiano
timeline.text: Caffè Guglielmo joins the Istituto Nazionale Espresso Italiano; a Guglielmo Point operates in Milan and a Rome branch opens.

timeline.title: 70 years
timeline.text: The company celebrates 70 years of activity.

timeline.title: From Calabria to Asia
timeline.text: First Guglielmo café in China (Qingdao, February), 13 franchised cafés in South Korea (April), 14 Guglielmo Stores in Italy, and an exclusive distribution deal for Vietnam (September).

timeline.title: Gusto capsules
timeline.text: March 2018: launch of Gusto capsules compatible with Nescafé Dolce Gusto machines, completing Guglielmo's compatible-capsule range, sold in supermarkets and the 14 Guglielmo Stores.

timeline.title: 80 years
timeline.text: Eighty years since 1943; U.S. Catanzaro co-branded capsules arrive in the US (L'Espresso USA catalog, 2023).

blends.name: Extra Bar
blends.composition: Arabica and Robusta blend ("the perfect blend of Arabica and Robusta" - official partner). Percentages not published. CONFLICT: Guglielmo Store Lamezia describes the beans as 100% Robusta - UNVERIFIED.
blends.intensity_source: PROPOSED (official partner tags it "Intensità forte" / strong)
notes: refined aroma with decisive notes (official store)
blends.crema: Dense, excellent texture (L'Espresso USA: "excellent cream texture")
blends.color_note: Matte black pack with gold/cream lettering
blends.description: The house blend of the Southern Italian espresso bar. Extra Bar pairs Arabica with Robusta for a dense crema, an intense aroma and a bold, cocoa-dark finish that stands up to milk. One of Guglielmo's longest-running blends, refined over the decades and made for the espresso machine and the moka pot alike.
blends.certification: Extra Bar beans certified "Espresso Italiano" by INEI (Annex 33, Cert. 214) per Guglielmo USA site - current status UNVERIFIED

blends.name: 5 Stelle (Bar 5 Stelle)
blends.composition: Arabica-led: Central American and Brazilian Arabica plus "other select top quality beans" (L'Espresso USA). Guglielmo Store: "best origins of Arabica and Robusta". Percentages not published.
blends.origins: Central America, Brazil (L'Espresso USA); an older Guglielmo text cites African and Central American origins (eccellenzecalabresi.it).
blends.roast: Dark ("tostatura spinta", eccellenzecalabresi.it), softened by long, progressive roast cycles (retailer sheet).
blends.intensity_source: PROPOSED (official partner: "media" for moka grind, "forte" for espresso grind)
notes: delicate yet intense, with a vein of sweetness (L'Espresso USA)
blends.color_note: Bronze-brown 1 kg bag / dark brown pouches, five gold stars, pink script logotype
blends.description: Five stars, one cup. Bar 5 Stelle blends Central American and Brazilian Arabica with other select origins, roasted slowly for a full, rounded body and a ribbon of sweetness. Delicate yet intense, with soft floral aromatics, it shines as a straight espresso and comes ground for the moka pot or finer for the espresso machine.
formats: Capsules 20 and 150 (36 mm, 7 g, Espresso Point-compatible)

blends.name: Espresso Bar
blends.composition: Arabica and Robusta ("fine Arabica and Robusta" - official partner). Older Guglielmo text: Central American Arabica, African coffees and "the best Robusta" (eccellenzecalabresi.it). Percentages not published.
blends.origins: Central and South America (L'Espresso USA); Central America and Africa (eccellenzecalabresi.it).
notes: balance of strength and sweetness (L'Espresso USA)
blends.color_note: Black bag with a sepia vintage bar photograph
blends.description: Espresso Bar starts from the backbone of Espresso Classico and adds select Central and South American Arabicas for extra sweetness. The result is a balanced, approachable shot with silky crema and a gentle finish. Guglielmo designed it as a lighter blend for export markets and Northern Italy, which makes it an easy everyday house espresso.

blends.name: Espresso Classico
blends.composition: Robusta (African and Asian) plus Arabica (Central American and Brazilian) - Guglielmo description via eccellenzecalabresi.it; L'Espresso USA: "Robusta and Brazilian Arabica". Percentages not published.
blends.origins: Africa and Asia (Robusta); Brazil and Central America (Arabica).
blends.roast: Dark ("tostatura standard spinta"); official: "a marked roast, softened by long, progressive cycles".
blends.intensity_source: PROPOSED (official partner tags it "Intensità forte" / strong)
notes: decisive, intense and round (Guglielmo via eccellenzecalabresi.it)
blends.color_note: Black-to-deep-red gradient pack, gold serif type ("Gusto Classico")
blends.description: The blend that started the Guglielmo tradition and a staple in Southern Italian homes. Robusta from Africa and Asia meets sweet Brazilian and Central American Arabica in a deep roast built for the moka pot: intense, round and nutty, with generous crema and an aroma that fills the kitchen. Also excellent as a bar espresso.
formats: Espresso capsules 20 and 150 (36 mm, Espresso Point-compatible)

blends.name: Caffetteria
blends.composition: Arabica and Robusta blend - split not published (UNVERIFIED).
blends.origins: South America, Africa and Asia (L'Espresso USA).
blends.roast: Dark (PROPOSED); official: "particularly refined and artfully roasted".
blends.intensity_source: PROPOSED (official partner tags it "Intensità forte" / strong)
blends.color_note: Oxblood / burgundy bag with cream script
blends.description: Caffetteria is Guglielmo's boldest whole bean: South American, African and Asian origins roasted for a strong, decisive cup with thick, velvety crema. Baristas pull it on its own for a full-throttle espresso or use it to give lighter blends more punch, and some customers even brew it as drip for a distinctive mug.

blends.name: Copacabana
blends.composition: 20% Arabica / 80% Robusta (Caffè Guglielmo Switzerland, official partner product page).
blends.intensity_source: PROPOSED (official partner tags it "Intensità media", but the Robusta share suggests a stronger cup)
notes: a more delicate touch in an intense coffee (official partner)
blends.description: A sunny gold bag with serious character. Copacabana combines 20% Arabica with 80% Robusta for a rounded, harmonious cup that cuts cleanly through steamed milk, making it a natural for cappuccino and latte. Pull it straight for a robust espresso, or blend it in to give a softer coffee more backbone.

blends.name: Club 99
blends.composition: Prized Central American Arabica "with a complement of excellent Robusta coffee to make the crema even more intense" (official). Percentages not published.

blends.color_note: Chocolate brown with gold script and a sepia vintage-café medallion

Expect a sweet, fragrant cup with a smooth, creamy texture. It comes in a collectible pack, ground for the moka pot, and in Espresso Point-compatible capsules for the office.

blends.name: Silver Signature
blends.composition: Fine Arabica coffees (L'Espresso USA catalog); official: a selection of "the finest coffees in the world". Arabica share UNVERIFIED.

Fine Arabica coffees are roasted and ground Italian-style for an elegant, balanced cup with a delicate, refined aroma. Brew it in the moka pot or an espresso machine.

blends.name: Organic Espresso
blends.composition: 100% Arabica, certified organic ("Bioagricoop controlled and certified" - L'Espresso USA). Swiss partner: single-origin coffee grown organically in Central America.
blends.color_note: Deep forest-green tin with coffee-blossom illustration
blends.description: Guglielmo's organic espresso is 100% Arabica from certified organic agriculture, ground for the moka pot and sealed in a 250 g tin to keep it fresh. Expect a gentle, smooth cup with soft sweetness and low bitterness: an easy choice for anyone who prefers a lighter espresso without giving up its Italian character.

blends.name: Decaf (Espresso Decaffeinato)
blends.composition: 100% Arabica, caffeine below 0.10% (official); water-based decaffeination process (L'Espresso USA catalog). The 6 kg wholesale decaf is "specially blended for Guglielmo USA" - composition UNVERIFIED.

blends.description: All the ritual, none of the caffeine. Guglielmo's decaf is 100% Arabica, decaffeinated with a water-based process to below 0.10% caffeine, then roasted for a soft, persistent aroma and a smooth, sweet crema. It comes ground for the moka pot, as whole beans for the bar, and in capsules and ESE pods.

Each capsule fits Nespresso Original machines*, so a Calabrian espresso is one button away at home or in the office. (*Not affiliated with or endorsed by Nespresso.)

blends.name: ROSSO70
blends.composition: Arabica and Robusta "Gusto Classico" blend - split not published (UNVERIFIED); L'Espresso USA tags it to the Espresso Classico family.

Compatible with Nespresso Original machines*, it is the everyday capsule for anyone who likes coffee with conviction. (*Not affiliated with or endorsed by Nespresso.)

blends.composition: Central and South American beans (L'Espresso USA). Arabica share not stated. Roaster: L'Espresso USA drip line is "locally roasted in small batches" (not Guglielmo SpA) - roaster identity UNVERIFIED.

taglines: Il caffè che fa centro. The coffee that hits the spot.
Right on target, cup after cup.
From the Ionian coast to your cup.
Roasted in Calabria. Delivered from Boston.
Since 1943, aiming for the perfect cup.
Bullseye espresso, from bean to bar.

stories.title: Il bar, alla calabrese
stories.text: In Catanzaro the day runs on the bar. A quick "un caffè" at the counter before work, another after lunch, one more when a friend walks in. Guglielmo grew up inside that ritual: Guglielmo Papaleo opened his shop on Corso Mazzini with a single coffee machine, and by 1950 the first Guglielmo bar was pouring espresso for the city. Every blend we import still answers to that counter: short, intense, generous with crema, gone in three sips.

stories.title: The roastery on the Ionian coast
stories.text: Guglielmo roasts at Copanello di Stalettì, a few kilometers from Catanzaro, where the plant has overlooked the Ionian Sea since 1972. Sacks of green coffee from Brazil, Central America, Africa and Asia are cleaned and tasted before they go near a roaster. Each origin is roasted on its own, up to about 300 °C, until its oils and aroma open, and only then blended into Extra Bar, Classico or Club 99. The plant spans 10,000 square meters.

stories.title: From Corso Mazzini to Boston
stories.text: In 2000 Mimmo (Domenico) Elia began importing Caffè Guglielmo to Boston, bringing a Calabrian espresso to the restaurants, pastry shops and families of New England. What started as a small import company grew into L'Espresso USA: distributors in several states, Canada since 2003, and a service team that installs, repairs and lends machines. Today the same blends poured in Catanzaro reach counters from the North End to Belmont. The coffee comes from Copanello; the delivery, the training and the service calls come from Boston.

brasilena.title: Brasilena: Calabria's coffee soda
brasilena.maker: Acqua Calabria (Cristofaro family), plant at Monte Covello, Girifalco (province of Catanzaro). Not a Guglielmo product; imported and sold by L'Espresso USA.
facts: Sparkling soft drink made from an infusion of roasted coffee in Calabrian oligomineral water (Acqua Calabria); ingredients: water, sugar, coffee infusion (12%), carbon dioxide, flavorings (Cookist).

Origins in the 1930s, when the Cristofaro grandfather made a "gazzosa al caffè" in his small emporium in Girifalco, roasting the coffee himself (Gambero Rosso interview, via CalabriaMagnifica / Radio Food).

The Brasilena name was registered and industrial bottling began in the 1960s (Salvatore Cristofaro); the drink became a regional success in the 1980s; production at Monte Covello since 1982 (sources vary - UNVERIFIED exact years).
Formats: glass bottles of 18, 25 and 92 cl and a 25 cl slim can; US: 250 ml cans (single, 6, 24) and bottles (24).
Reported as Calabria's best-selling soft drink and recognized as a "Marchio Storico di Interesse Nazionale" in 2021 (Cookist / Radio Food - UNVERIFIED).
The vintage label features a smiling woman in a sombrero (illustration signed "R. Casaro" on the carton); the name is said to evoke South American coffee arriving in Calabrian ports (UNVERIFIED).
brasilena.story: Brasilena is what Calabria drinks when it is too late for an espresso and too early for an aperitivo. Born as a "gazzosa al caffè" in a 1930s village shop in Girifalco, it is still made by the Cristofaro family's Acqua Calabria: real coffee infused in Calabrian mineral water, lightly sparkling, bittersweet and served ice-cold. US tagline used on our site: "Brasilena, it sparkles your life."

voice.detail: Speak from real places and objects - Catanzaro, Copanello, the bar counter, the moka - instead of generic "old world" imagery.

voice.principle: Short and strong, like the espresso
voice.detail: Direct sentences, active verbs, no hype words (no "unforgettable", "world's best", "artisanal" without proof).
The welcome of a Calabrian bar: inclusive, generous, a little playful. Italian words sparingly, always clear from context.
Explain roast, grind and crema in plain English; give operators practical, specific guidance.
Only verifiable claims; name certifications and blends precisely; label compatibility claims and trademarks correctly.
Guglielmo speaks heritage and taste; Guglielmo USA speaks service and reliability (3-day delivery, loaner machines, on-site techs).
Use the "fa centro" / bullseye idea as a light motif, not in every headline.

colors.method: Logo colors read directly from the official SVG fills. Pack colors are median-cut samples from official packshots in assets/img/brand (lighting and print finish affect values; use as digital approximations).

typography_observed.wordmark: Custom stencil-cut, condensed, heavy display letterforms (GUGLIELMO) with a red dot over the i; not a retail font (UNVERIFIED name).
typography_observed.tagline: Clean, regular-weight sans-serif in red, lowercase ("il caffè che fa centro").
typography_observed.packaging: Each blend has its own display lettering: gold Didone-style serif (Extra Bar, Espresso Classico), retro pink script (Bar 5 Stelle), gold copperplate script (Club 99), art-deco caps (Copacabana), handwritten signature (Silver).
typography_observed.web_recommendation: PROPOSED: a condensed grotesk or stencil display for headlines (never re-set the logo), a high-contrast serif for blend names, a neutral sans for body copy.
